subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Agent Collaboration Enhancement: Capability Profiling + Shared Blackboard + Layered Memory + Token Cost Governance

question: Which part of the four-layer collaboration stack should OpenClaw core own first, and which parts should stay in plugins/ClawHub or narrower RFCs?
rationale: Current main only provides primitives, while the requested stack changes state storage, config, memory visibility, delegation authority, and budget enforcement across multiple owner boundaries.

options.title: Keep canonical and split
options.body: Keep #35203 open as the umbrella and require narrower accepted issues or PRs for each layer with explicit security and upgrade criteria.

options.title: Sponsor one core substrate
options.body: Choose one minimal core substrate such as a typed capability index or scoped meeting lifecycle, while deferring blackboard, memory promotion, and budget policy.

options.title: Route optional orchestration outward
options.body: Direct blackboard, learned routing, and memory orchestration experiments to plugins or ClawHub until a missing core API is proven.

recommendation.title: Keep canonical and split
recommendation.body: Keep #35203 open as the umbrella and require narrower accepted issues or PRs for each layer with explicit security and upgrade criteria.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across subagent runtime, capability-profile, registry, session-visibility, and docs surfaces implicated by the RFC.
